operator_io_quirks: journal_committee is a junction table: composite PK (Editor_ID, Journal_ID) and two FKs to editor/journal; both PK members are also FK children.
All PK columns declared int but NOT NULL flag is 0 (notnull=0) on every column; sqlite PK still enforces uniqueness but allows NULL in non-INTEGER-PK composite.
journal.Date is TEXT storing human dates like 'September 9, 2001' (month-name format), not ISO; declared type TEXT so TS dispatches to String, not Date.
journal.Theme holds free text with leading 'at ' prefixes and team names; distinct=16 equals row count (all unique).
editor.Name has non-ASCII (Polish) characters (Pręgowski); String fuzzer CHARSET is ASCII-only so fresh names lose diacritics.
editor.Age declared REAL, storage real, values are whole floats (34.0); Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) -> default scale.
journal.Sales INT with values up to 7494; Number fuzzer range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from 'int' (no args) may be narrow.
journal_committee.Work_Type has only 3 distinct values (Photo/Article/Title) over 7 rows; low-cardinality text.
All tables tiny (16/9/7 rows); original_values sampling k=min(5,len) will use most of each column.
FK parent columns (editor.Editor_ID, journal.Journal_ID) are single-column PKs, so parent values are unique; child draws with replacement can duplicate.
journal_committee.Editor_ID distinct=6 < editor rows 9 and Journal_ID distinct=7 < journal rows 16: not all parents referenced.
No views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs; DDL uses backtick-quoted parent refs in FK clauses.
operator_ts_expectations: journal.Date -> String fuzzer (declared TEXT): fresh random ASCII strings + contaminate, NOT date-shaped; gold queries comparing dates/ordering will see implausible values -> likely FN.
journal.Theme -> String: random strings, loses 'at ' prefix structure and team-name semantics -> FN on LIKE/prefix predicates.
editor.Name -> String: ASCII random strings, no diacritics, no name shape -> FN on name predicates.
editor.Age -> Number(real): floats in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-0.01/0.02 perturbation; may produce negative or huge ages -> FN on age range predicates.
journal.Sales -> Number(int): ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] perturbed +-1/2; scale from bare 'int' likely small -> values may not reach 7494 -> FN on Sales thresholds.
All PKs -> Number with single-column PK max_l0=inf (journal, editor) so fresh draws unbounded; composite PK members capped at 30.

journal_committee FK columns draw from parent FINAL filtered values with replacement; composite PK dedup then drops duplicate (Editor_ID,Journal_ID) rows -> ties/duplicates reduced -> FP on COUNT/DISTINCT queries.
Work_Type -> String: 3 originals + pool; fresh random strings dominate -> FN on Work_Type='Article' style predicates.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; rows violating PK/unique dropped at insert -> smaller tables, missing ties -> FP on aggregate/join-count queries.
Date column being TEXT means TS never uses Date fuzzer here; any gold query with date literals gets no date-shaped pool values -> FN.
Tiny tables: choose_table_sizes may produce sizes far from 16/9/7, changing join cardinalities -> FP/FN on count-sensitive queries.
FK consistency holds (parents exist, unique) so join queries won't spuriously empty; misses come from value implausibility, not referential breakage.
